title: Sleeping Beauty

story_parts.intro: Once, in a sunlit kingdom by the sea, where olive trees danced on rolling hills and jasmine perfumed the warm breeze, a baby girl was born to the King and Queen. Her name was Aurora. The whitewashed palace with blue doors and zellige tiles glowed with joy. In the courtyard, neighbors gathered around a hand-carved cradle. There was couscous, brik, dates, and mint tea. Musicians played the oud and darbuka. Flora, Fauna, and Merryweather, the three guardian fairies, came in colorful scarves and simple robes. They spoke blessings over Aurora with jasmine flowers and sweet offerings. 'May she be kind. May she be brave. May she be loved.' But then the sky darkened. Maleficent appeared, angry that she had not been invited. She pointed a long finger at the cradle and cursed: 'Before the sun sets on her sixteenth birthday, Aurora shall prick her finger on a spinning wheel spindle and fall into a deep sleep.' The hall grew cold. Merryweather stepped forward and softened the curse: 'She will not die. She will sleep until true love's kiss wakes her.' The King and Queen trembled, and the fairies promised to protect Aurora.
story_parts.developpement: To keep Aurora safe, Flora, Fauna, and Merryweather carried her far from the palace to a hidden palm oasis. There, among date palms and fig trees, stood a small whitewashed farmhouse. They raised her as Briar Rose, a cheerful girl with an embroidered dress and silver bracelets. She learned to tend the olive grove, bake bread in the shared oven, and fetch cool water. The fairies sang soft lullabies under brass lanterns. Years passed, and Aurora grew kind and brave. On the morning of her sixteenth birthday, she was still fifteen for only a few more hours. The fairies were busy preparing a birthday feast of figs, pomegranates, and almond sweets. A strange shimmering light led Aurora away from the oasis, through a gate of cactus and bougainvillea, to a high tower in the palace. There she found a carved wooden spinning wheel. She had never seen one before. Curious, she touched the spindle. A sharp point pricked her finger. A sleepy mist filled the room. Aurora fell into a deep, enchanted sleep. Flora, Fauna, and Merryweather found her, and with gentle magic they laid her in a quiet room, guarded by jasmine and lantern light.
story_parts.conclusion: Prince Phillip loved Aurora. He had met her in the oasis and carried her kindness in his heart. When he learned what had happened, he rode to the palace. A thick wall of cactus and thorny bougainvillea had grown around it, sharp and tangled. He pushed through bravely, his ceremonial vest torn, his riding boots dusty. Inside the courtyard, Maleficent rose before him. She transformed into a great dragon, with scales like dark stone and eyes like fire. Phillip battled her with courage and a shining sword. Flora, Fauna, and Merryweather helped him with blessings of strength and light. At last, he defeated Maleficent. The dragon vanished, and the cactus wall softened. Phillip climbed the tower and found Aurora sleeping. He knelt beside her and kissed her gently. True love's kiss broke the curse. Aurora opened her eyes and smiled. The whole kingdom woke with her. There was music, mint tea, and shared sweets. Aurora was reunited with her family, and the fairies blessed her again. And everyone learned that true love, kindness, and courage can overcome even the darkest curses.
